Repository audit -- P100 SeedAudit

A committed numeric claim is a numeric token in a committed output file beside the script that produced it, where that script declares a rewritable random seed. Each candidate is run twice in two separate pristine copies: PERTURBED, with every seed literal rewritten, and CONTROL, with the seeds left alone. A number that moves in the perturbed run and not in the control is seed-attributable and is the headline. A number that moves in the control was never reproducible at its declared seed and is counted separately. Detection power is 1-(1-p)^n against a committed reference and 1-p^n-(1-p)^n for run-and-diff with no reference; a clean result reports the escaped-rate upper bound 1-alpha^(1/n), never zero.

==============================================================================
3b. THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN FOOTPRINT, excluded from the headline
==============================================================================
a script that prints its own seed reports a changed number in the
perturbed run for one reason: the audit changed the seed. The control
cannot absorb it, because in the control the seed is unchanged. Counting
it as a finding would be the audit reporting its own perturbation back to
itself, which is the self-polluting-check class one level up.

7. WHAT THIS RUN DOES NOT CLAIM
==============================================================================
a candidate reported as compared with no moved numbers is evidence that this ONE perturbed seed draw did not move it. It is not evidence that no seed does, and it is not evidence about intermittency at a fixed seed: that is the repeat axis and this run samples it once per arrangement, bound 0.95.
the committed output artifact is deleted inside the pristine copy before each run, so a script that does not rewrite it is reported as no_output rather than compared against itself. That deletion applies identically to the control run, so it cannot reach the headline.
